title: KV page fingerprinting and staggered decode controller for paged-attention
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We observe tail latency spikes and elevated eviction churn when the KV cache is populated by many small, semantically-similar pages that cannot be coalesced by the current allocator strategy. This ticket pilots two coordinated techniques: (1) lightweight page fingerprinting + binning to increase co-location and reuse of similar KV pages and reduce fragmentation; (2) a staggered decode/prefill controller that spaces decode waves based on bin saturation and kernel selection heuristics to avoid simultaneous heavy prefill pressure on the serving runtime. The goal is to improve effective KV hit rate, reduce background eviction thrashing, and enable the runtime to pick more efficient fused kernels for hot working sets.
motivation: Reduce 95/99P decode latency, improve token cost by lowering redundant prefill work, and stabilize GPU memory pressure across multi-tenant workloads. This is especially important for Dedicated customers with constrained capacity and for hosted users with bursty request patterns.
design_summary: 1) Fingerprint & Bin Allocator: compute a compact fingerprint for each incoming prefill candidate page based on hash of recent token-id patterns, request fingerprint, and a lightweight sketch of KV key distribution. Use deterministic bin assignment (16 bins per shard) to place pages into logical bins; allocator prefers placing new allocations into partially-filled bins with compatible page shapes. Eviction logic becomes bin-aware: when reclaiming, prefer evicting from least-recently-used bins with low reuse score. 2) Staggered Decode Controller: controller monitors per-bin saturation (% pages in-resident) and schedules decode/prefill waves with per-bin backoff timers to avoid waves overlapping across bins that would otherwise cause synchronous kernel pressure. Controller also emits a kernel-selection hint: when a bin's hit-rate > threshold, prefer fused-attention kernel variants; when mixing cold/warm pages in a work-queue, use chunked kernels with lower memory spikes. 3) Integration with kernel selector: extend kernel catalog to attach hints (memory footprint, warm-path score) and allow the scheduler to query expected post-prefill residency to choose kernels conservatively for mixed waves.
tradeoffs:
- Fingerprint collisions: using compact fingerprints reduces metadata cost but risks bin pollution. We'll mitigate with periodic re-evaluation and move heuristics.
- Latency vs throughput: staggering prefills smooths spikes but can slightly increase median prefill latency for some requests; we cap stagger windows to bound added latency.
- Complexity: bin-aware eviction adds bookkeeping; we must ensure metadata overhead is <1% of total KV memory.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation shows >=15% relative reduction in eviction churn on synthetic mixed workloads (kvsim-v2).
95P decode tail latency reduced by >=10% on our internal steady-state benchmark (gpt-like workloads).
KV hit-rate increase of >=12 percentage points on representative PLG traffic traces without increasing avg mem usage >5%.
No regression (>3%) in median latency for cold-start prefill requests in end-to-end QA harness.
Design doc + API changes reviewed and approved by runtime/infra leads; PR in codebase with unit + integration tests merged.
simulation_results: kvsim-v2 (mixed-tenancy trace): baseline eviction churn 0.42 evict/sec -> prototype 0.31 evict/sec (-26%); KV hit-rate baseline 62% -> prototype 78% (+16pp). Tail (95P) decode latency: baseline 48ms -> prototype 39.2ms (-18%); median decode latency: 12.4ms -> 13.1ms (+5%) due to controlled staggering. GPU mem fragmentation metric (compaction passes) decreased by 21%. All numbers from 1000-run bootstrap with 4 shards, A100-equivalent profile.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): implement compact fingerprint generator and deterministic binning; add in-memory per-bin accounting and unit tests. Phase 2 (3 wks): implement staggered decode controller and kernel-selection hook; run kvsim benchmarks and flamegraphs. Phase 3 (1 wk): integrate bin-aware eviction policy and low-overhead metrics. Phase 4 (1 wk): staged rollout behind feature flag to canary cluster; monitor evictions, hit-rate, tail latency. Phase 5 (contingent): refine thresholds and add dynamic bin resizing if needed.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout to canary (10% traffic) -> observe for 48 hours -> expand to Dedicated-only clusters for 72 hours -> full cluster rollout. Emergency kill switch: disable controller and revert allocator to previous deterministic round-robin placement. Dashboard will expose per-bin saturation, prefill backoff rate, and kernel-choice histogram.
monitoring: New metrics: bin_saturation{shard,bin}, prefill_backoff_seconds, kernel_hint_chosen, bin_eviction_count, bin_reuse_score. Alert if 95P decode latency increases >10% or eviction_churn increases >15% vs baseline. Add SLO dashboard and link to console runtime-1.20 release page.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fingerprint-induced misplacement of heterogeneous pages can hurt reuse. Mitigation: conservative fingerprint (include request-level salt) and probation period where pages can be migrated between bins when reuse score is low.
Risk: Staggering may increase cold-request latency. Mitigation: bounded backoff window (max 30ms) and opt-out for latency-sensitive routes (tagged in request metadata).
Risk: Added metadata memory. Mitigation: store compact counters (u16/u32) with periodic compaction; disable on low-memory tiers.
notes: Prototype microbench implemented in branch feature/kv-fingerprint-bins; initial perf tests ran on internal perf cluster cpusim-6 with simulated GPUs.
